source.title: Simplicity bias and optimization threshold in two-layer ReLU networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The text includes the main paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own two-layer network training results, showing that training can fail to interpolate in a specific noisy regression setting despite overparameterization. This qualifies the broader training-error claim, but it does not test the listed classification, teacher-student width, depth, initialization, learning-rate, or batch-normalization versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper studies noisy regression, not classification benchmarks. It reports text-described training-loss outcomes for its own experiments; cited results about diffusion and in-context learning are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study reports regression interpolation and non-interpolation in shallow networks. None of V1–V6 names this result: V1 concerns convolutional classification, V2 concerns matched teacher/student width and extra neurons, and V3–V6 concern depth, initialization-dependent speed, stability thresholds, or normalization. The regression findings do not test those versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. Under restrictive data and small-initialization assumptions, gradient flow converges to a non-global solution formed from OLS fits on two input subsets. Experiments show related non-interpolation with good test performance under broader regression setups. The authors leave the mechanism in complex architectures unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses two-layer networks on noisy regression with squared loss, not the listed classification benchmarks or interventions. Main experiments use SGD and small Gaussian initialization; appendices also report GeLU and Adam experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The interpolation threshold changes with sample count and dimension; the paper reports later transitions for d = 10 and for the five-ReLU teacher. The GeLU experiment is unable to interpolate at n = 500, and Adam gives similar final results to the GeLU experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: The fixed-width ReLU regression network interpolates at n = 500 but fails to interpolate at n = 5,000; transition locations change with dimension and teacher complexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small-initialization two-layer networks can fail to interpolate noisy regression data despite sufficient representational capacity, with outcomes depending on sample count and data model.

fits_no_version.finding: The 10,000-neuron GeLU network fails to interpolate even at n = 500, and Adam produces similar final results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large finite width and Adam do not guarantee interpolation in the tested small-initialization GeLU regression setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Warm-restarted training reduces loss only from about 0.082 to slightly above 0.0815 while the learning rate decays to approximately 10^-8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing the learning rate after convergence need not restore interpolation in the reported noisy regression setting.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The theoretical result uses a restrictive linear data model and assumptions on the data and initialization. Main experiments use d = 5 and fixed width m = 10 000; several transitions are described approximately from figures. The experiments do not address classification.
record.rows_left_out: No additional distinct text-described training-error outcomes were omitted. Figures 2, 4, 5, 7, and 8 plot loss across sample counts, but the text does not provide exact per-sample-count values beyond the approximate thresholds recorded above.

untested.parts: All: convolutional classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels and the stated training recipes.
All: spurious-minimum frequency as teacher and student widths grow together, and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
All: depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization and normalization exceptions.
All: activation-matched initialization effects on training speed and depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
All: learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss recovery, sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
All: batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: T5 requires an argument or result against a listed version; opposition to a broader interpolation assumption is insufficient. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6, while the regression outcomes remain valid findings under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and the stated SGD/Adam classification recipes.
Teacher-student problems, spurious-local-minimum frequency as teacher and student widths grow, and comparisons giving the student extra neurons.
Depth, plain versus residual shortcuts, batch-normalized convolutional networks, and the cited special cases.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and convolutional networks at 10,000 layers.
Learning rates relative to a stability threshold, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence rates.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network (m = 10 000)
rows.operation_detail: SGD training on the linear regression model with n = 500 samples

conditions.value: linear model with centered Gaussian inputs and centered Gaussian noise of variance σ² = 0.09

rows.value: interpolation of the training data happens
rows.note: The paper describes this smaller-sample setting as interpolating at convergence; this is regression loss, not classification error.
rows.check: Interpolation at n = 500 is correctly reported, but regression interpolation does not measure any listed version. The initialization variance is inconsistent within the source: Section 5 gives 10^-5/m, whereas Appendix A.1 prints 10^-5/sqrt(m).

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network (m = 10 000)
rows.operation_detail: SGD training on the linear regression model with n = 5 000 samples

conditions.value: linear model with centered Gaussian inputs and centered Gaussian noise of variance σ² = 0.09

rows.baseline: OLS training loss is slightly larger than the network's training loss
rows.value: interpolation of the training data does not happen anymore
rows.locator: Section 5; Figure 2(a); Section 5.1; Figure 3(b); Appendix A.1
rows.note: Authors state this setting is beyond the optimization threshold; nearly all neurons align with OLS, but a few misaligned neurons slightly improve training loss.
rows.check: Non-interpolation at n = 5,000 is correctly reported, but does not establish absence of any listed effect. The same initialization-variance inconsistency applies.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network (m = 10 000)
rows.operation_detail: SGD training on the linear regression model as sample count varies

conditions.value: linear model; setup as Appendix A.1 with dimension changed to d = 10
interpolation stops around n = 10 000; an estimate close to OLS starts around n = 80 000

rows.value: interpolation stops happening around n = 10 000 samples
rows.note: The text gives approximate transition points and says the OLS-like estimate begins at a substantially larger sample count.
rows.check: The approximate transition points are correctly reported. A transition across sample counts is not a partial instance of any listed version; separate interpolating and non-interpolating conditions if retaining regression-specific states.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network (m = 10 000)
rows.operation_detail: Training with a five-ReLU teacher as sample count varies

conditions.value: linear-model inputs and noise; labels generated by a five-ReLU teacher
interpolation does not happen anymore around n = 2 000; training and testing losses close to noise variance around n⋆ = 17 000

rows.value: interpolation is reached for small n, then is not reached after a threshold
rows.note: Authors state the transition is slower than for the linear teacher and requires more samples for both losses to approach the noise variance.
rows.check: This noisy five-ReLU teacher experiment varies sample count with a fixed 10,000-neuron student. It does not test V2's matched-width growth or benefit from one or two extra neurons. The row combines interpolating and non-interpolating conditions.

rows.subject: two-layer GeLU network (m = 10 000)
rows.size_stated: m = 10 000 neurons; dimension not stated in the excerpt
rows.operation_detail: Training with GeLU activation as sample count varies

conditions.value: network is already unable to interpolate for n = 500

rows.value: even very wide networks are far from interpolation; unable to interpolate for n = 500
rows.note: The authors describe this as surprising and suggest the activation's near-linearity around the origin may make noisy-label fitting harder.
rows.check: GeLU non-interpolation at n = 500 is correctly reported but measures no listed version. The inherited experimental dimension is d = 5.

rows.subject: two-layer GeLU network trained with Adam

rows.value: observed results are very similar to Figure 4; the network does not interpolate for large sample counts

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network (m = 10 000)
rows.stage_stated: warm restart from training at n = 8 000; continued for 4 × 10^6 iterations
rows.operation_detail: Continued training with a decaying learning-rate schedule

conditions.value: same training dataset as the n = 8 000 Figure 2 experiment
multiply learning rate by 0.85 every 50 000 iterations; final learning rate of order 10−8

rows.baseline: around 0.082 at the end of initial training
rows.note: The paper says loss does not change much and interprets this as convergence to a spurious stationary point rather than instability. This is a continued-training comparison, not a classification result.
rows.check: The loss values and schedule match the text. No initial linearized stability threshold or curvature trajectory is measured, so this does not test V5. The authors describe the loss reduction as small.
